quizName: Hardest Questions in Kentucky Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: As much as a face shield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: How can you help others see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright colors, use your headlight all the time, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It is too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear it while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. In warm weather, leather jackets keep you cool and help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you comfortable in hot weather.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle. It contains information about how it works and what maintenance it needs.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing someone else's motorcycle.

questions.question: How do you get the most protection from a helmet?

options.text: Use a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
Use a helmet that survived a crash.
Use a helmet with hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.
Ask your friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Stop them from riding. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What material are riding gloves usually made of?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: You should check your mirrors:

options.text: As part of your regular scanning routine.
Never, since you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal driving routine. Use them before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can force you into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is safe because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can force you into another lane.
questions.explanation: Going too fast around a corner may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn or go through a curve.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:

options.text: Be worn in and broken in.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It must fit snugly all around your head and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: What fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A car door may open or a driver may pull out into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly while looking for a spot.
The road surface may be rough.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car door may open or a driver may pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is risky. A driver might suddenly pull out without looking. Car doors can open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: For the best protection, your boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover your ankle and give support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankle and give support.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle's parts.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have which types of brakes?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for new riders.
Helps new riders practice in different situations.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What should you check before each ride?

options.text: How much cushion your seat has

questions.explanation: Before you ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Inspect your tires, oil and fluids, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a motorcycle must have a rearview mirror, headlight with high and low beams, taillight, horn, muffler and tailpipe, brake light, front and rear brakes, and good tires. It must also be registered and have liability insurance.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Limits your movement to one area of the lane.
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to drive faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space on all sides of your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road all provide poor grip. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet must:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good method.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A visual check is not enough because an under-inflated tire can still look normal.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery. Ride with caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend in and avoid being noticed by other drivers.
Use turn signals only at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers may keep you awake but cannot reduce your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A proper fit means your feet can reach the ground while seated. You should also be able to easily reach and operate all controls.
